sections.html:
Farragut is a suburban town in Knox County with a small extension into Loudon County, part of the Knoxville metro area. It covers 16.2 square miles. Interstate 40/75 forms most of the northern edge, Turkey Creek Road and the Norfolk Southern rail line mark the south, the Loudon County line is the west boundary, and Lovell Road plus the Concord Hills subdivisions close off the east.

The 2020 census counted 23,506 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 25,121, a gain of 6.9 percent. Of 8,992 housing units, 5.2 percent sat vacant, with a 1.5 percent vacancy rate among owner homes and 14.3 percent among rentals. Few owner homes sit empty, which is useful context when you weigh a sale.

Farragut sits in hilly ground between Blackoak Ridge to the north and Fort Loudoun Lake on the Tennessee River to the south. Hills mean sloped lots, and sloped lots mean buyers and inspectors pay attention to drainage, retaining walls and foundations.

Annual precipitation is 47.86 inches. Nearly 48 inches of rain a year puts roofs, gutters and crawl spaces on every inspection list. A seller who has patched a leak or regraded a yard should keep the receipts for the buyer. Walk the property after a storm and write down where water collects, since an honest note about drainage reads better to a buyer than a surprise in the inspection report. Retaining walls and foundations on sloped lots deserve the same treatment, with any contractor invoices attached.

Farragut levies no municipal property tax. Residents pay the Knox County rate of $1.55 per $100 of assessed value, with homes assessed at 25 percent of market value and commercial property at 40 percent. Your actual bill is on the trustee's site. Knox County sales tax is 9.25 percent, or 5.25 percent on groceries.

The Knox County Property Assessor reappraises on a two-year schedule and mails a notice whenever an assessed value changes. If you disagree with a value, the County Board of Equalization hears appeals in June. After a deed is recorded, the assessor's system can take up to a week to show the new owner.

Farragut's Building and Fire Codes Division enforces the building, plumbing, gas, mechanical, housing, swimming pool and fire codes. A permit is needed for most remodeling. Water heater change-outs, HVAC replacements and any gas appliance installation require permits and inspections through the Town, and mechanical applications must include a Manual J report. Electrical inspections run through the Lenoir City Utilities Board.

Work that skips a permit is the usual snag at closing, so confirm what was permitted before listing. Items on the Town's no-permit list include one-story detached sheds up to 200 square feet and fences up to 7 feet, though zoning approval may still apply.

• A complaint is reviewed and an officer does a drive-by inspection.
  • A courtesy notice goes to the owner, usually with a 10-day deadline, though it can range from immediate to 30 days.
  • If the problem persists, the owner can be cited to Municipal Court, where fines reach $50 per day per violation.
  • The Town may fix the problem itself and place a lien on the property for the cost.

If you have an open notice, call Town Hall at 865-966-7057 before accepting any offer, because a lien would have to be dealt with at closing.

sections.h2: Schools, roads and utilities buyers ask about
sections.html:
Most Farragut addresses are zoned to Knox County Schools: Farragut Primary (K-2), Farragut Intermediate (3-5), Farragut Middle (6-8) and Farragut High (9-12), with Northshore Elementary also serving the area. Part of the town north of I-75 is zoned for Hardin Valley Middle and Hardin Valley Academy.

Kingston Pike runs through the middle of town and I-40/75 runs along its northern edge. A commuter lot at Campbell Station Road and Campbell Lakes Drive serves ride sharers. Gas comes from the Knoxville Utilities Board, electricity from the Lenoir City Utility Board, and fire protection is subscription-based through Rural Metro. A buyer who learns about the Rural Metro subscription early will not be surprised by it at closing. Tell buyers early which utility serves the house, and mention the commuter lot if your street is near it. Concrete details like these make a listing sheet or a seller's note more useful than general praise for the neighborhood.

sections.h2: From offer to recorded deed in Farragut
sections.html:
Your options are an agent listing, a direct sale to a buyer, or a cash offer from a company that takes houses as they stand. Cash suits a house with deferred work, a code notice or a firm deadline. Any route ends with the deed recorded in Knox County, not at Town Hall.

Record the deed promptly, even though no statutory time limit exists. Signatures need a notary or two witnesses, and documents are usually recorded the day they arrive. The realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of the purchase price, paid by the grantee when the deed is recorded.

The assessor will send a sales questionnaire after ownership changes, including a private sale or a transfer into a trust. Tell the trustee where to mail later bills, and ask the Knox County Trustee how any current-year balance is handled at closing.

sections.h2: Steps before you accept an offer
sections.html: Start with your permit records, and ask Community Development if a notice is open on the property. Next, line up the deed, any payoff letter and your newest tax bill. Everyone on the deed needs to be able to sign in front of a notary or two witnesses. Even a buyer who takes the house as it is will want an open notice or a missing permit cleared, because a lien or an unpermitted water heater swap can stall closing. Ask the closing company for the full settlement statement the day before, and read it with the tax bill beside you. That small habit catches most surprises.

faqs.q: Does Farragut have its own property tax?
faqs.a: No municipal tax is levied by the Town of Farragut. Homeowners pay the Knox County rate of $1.55 per $100 of assessed value, on 25 percent of market value.

faqs.q: Where is a Farragut deed recorded?
faqs.a: The Knox County Register of Deeds takes it, at 400 Main Street, Suite 225, Knoxville (865-215-2330). Each county records only property inside its own borders.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a water heater in Farragut?
faqs.a: Yes. The Town of Farragut requires a permit and inspection for water heater change-outs, HVAC replacements and gas appliance installations. Contact the Codes office at 865-966-7057 or 865-675-2384 if you are unsure.

faqs.q: What happens if Farragut sends me a code courtesy notice before I sell?
faqs.a: Respond before the deadline, usually 10 days. If the issue is still open at the follow-up inspection, the owner can be cited to Municipal Court, with fines up to $50 per day per violation, and the Town can place a lien after fixing the problem.

faqs.q: Which side pays transfer tax in Farragut?
faqs.a: The buyer, as grantee, owes $0.37 per $100 of purchase price at recording. The Register of Deeds collects it for the state.
